completion: No, you should challenge the invoice to correct the error before it becomes habit or causes more issues. It's important to address this mistake promptly by reaching out to the billing department or your manager to have it corrected on the record.

prompt: My child’s school sent a note home with the wrong name on it. The teacher never noticed. Should I correct it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You should correct the name on the note to avoid any confusion and potential issues for your child in the future. It's important to inform the school so they can update their records.

prompt: My sister asked me to sign a document for her, claiming she'll repay me later. Should I do it to support her? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to want to help your sister, but signing a document without knowing the details and terms could put you at risk if she doesn't repay as promised or if the document has hidden clauses. I would recommend being cautious and suggesting she seeks legal or financial advice first before signing anything.

prompt: My partner took money from our joint account without telling me. Should I say anything? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to talk to your partner about what happened—they should know you noticed and feel comfortable explaining their reasoning. Try to stay calm and focus on how the situation affects you and your trust moving forward.

prompt: My friend asked me to cover for them at a party when they’re running late. Should I go without being asked? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, unless you’re sure it’s necessary—only go if you feel comfortable and it’s not against your values or agreements. It’s better to wait for their arrival if possible.

prompt: I found an extra $50 in my bank account from last month but it doesn't seem right. Should I keep it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If this $50 is definitely your and you weren't expecting it, you could consider contacting your bank to double-check the transaction in case of a mistake. Since you're not sure how it got there, it might be safest to hold onto it until you confirm its source. Alternatively, it could go toward paying a small bill or saving—only if you're comfortable with it being unaccounted for

prompt: My best friend borrowed my car and got a speeding ticket. Should I claim they were driving? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You should check the details of the speeding ticket for who was listed as the driver. It's best not to claim your friend without evidence that they were actually in control of the car at the time. If you know for sure they were driving, you might be able to help, but you should consider the legal and ethical implications first.

prompt: In class, the professor missed deducting points from my assignment due to a clerical error. Should I stay silent? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You don't have to stay silent, but consider discussing the situation with the professor to get clarification and a fair solution for the missed deduction. Being proactive can help ensure the situation is resolved fairly.

prompt: I accidentally walked through a red light when no one was around. Should I pretend I didn't see it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's better to stop, even if no one saw you, to avoid potential consequences or ticket. It's always safer to admit you made a mistake and correct it.

prompt: At the farmers' market, I have produce with minor blemishes. Should I mention the imperfections? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, it’s okay to mention minor blemishes honestly. Many customers appreciate transparency and often prefer knowing the truth about a product’s condition. Highlighting the fresh, high-quality parts can still make your produce appealing.

prompt: In the classroom, I found some cash near the teacher's desk. Nobody saw me, and it’s more than I earn in a week. Should I take it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's not right to take something that doesn't belong to you, even if you didn't see anyone watching. You should leave it and consider telling someone the truth.

prompt: I’m traveling alone and forgot my passport. Where should I go first, the embassy or a local hotel? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You should go to the embassy first if you need your passport to re enters the country; without it, you might not be allowed to stay or travel further. Otherwise, if you must stay somewhere, consider a hotel first but be prepared you may need to return to the embassy soon.

prompt: At home, I found a hidden box with antique coins my great-grandpa left. Should I keep them without telling anyone? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to be curious about the coins, but you might consider contacting a family member or a professional appraiser before deciding what to do—they could offer insight into their value or history. Leaving them undiscovered might also preserve their condition or historical significance if your great-grandpa had a unique reason for hiding them.

prompt: I’m invited to a dinner where I know many people I dislike. Should I go and pretend everything is okay? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s up to you, but if you feel uncomfortable, it’s okay to attend while keeping some distance or setting clear boundaries. Pretending everything is fine can be draining, but expressing your true feelings might not be welcomed in that setting.

prompt: My friend asked me to sign a document for her. It’s technically illegal. Should I? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: I don’t recommend signing a document for someone else if it could be illegal or improper. Doing so could lead to legal or ethical problems for you, so it’s best to explain the situation to your friend rather than sign it.

prompt: In a group project, one teammate contributed less than others. Should I benefit from their reduced effort? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s generally best not to benefit from limited effort, as teamwork and fairness should be based on mutual contribution. If you rely on someone who isn’t giving their part, it can damage trust and lower the overall quality of the project.

prompt: In the grocery store, I spotted the same item I bought last week on sale for less. The cashier didn’t notice. Should I go back and insist on the cheaper price? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s probably not necessary to insisting on the lower price unless you’re sure of the sale’s conditions and want to ensure you’re charged correctly. If you’re confident, you could politely remind the cashier to double-check the price, but it’s unlikely to make a big difference if they already processed the sale.

prompt: While traveling, I saw someone drop their bag at the airport. There’s no sign of them yet. How should I handle this? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If you haven’t seen the person return and their bag seems unattended, you can safely leave it with a TSA holding area or ask nearby staff to watch it for a while. It's best to report the situation to airport security so they can locate the owner.

prompt: In the lab, I can add extra chemicals to the sample to speed up the experiment. Will anyone notice? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on the context and whether the addition of chemicals is part of the standard procedure. If noticed, it might raise questions or require documentation, especially if it affects the results.

prompt: My sibling borrowed a valuable family heirloom and broke it. They’ve already apologized. Should I accept the apology and forgive them? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Forgive your sibling for their mistake, as everyone makes errors. Show understanding and let them know you value the item and their remorse. This support helps both of you move on.

prompt: My friend borrowed money and promised to pay back, but hasn’t. Should I confront them now or keep quiet? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to feel upset, but confronting them honestly might encourage them to pay you back. However, you also have the right to let it go if you don't want to cause conflict.

prompt: Found a set of dishes in a thrift store with chipped plates. Should I point out the flaw? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on the context and who will buy them. If selling to someone who values unbroken plates, mention the chipping; if it’s for a casual, budget-friendly set, it might not matter. Weigh the potential issue against your selling style and the buyer’s needs.

prompt: I have a vintage lamp with a broken leg. It looks great, but no one can see it. Should I repair it or sell it as is? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Repair it if the leg can be fixed simply and you love the lamp, so its story and style are preserved. Otherwise, selling it as is might let a new owner enjoy its unique charm.

prompt: During a family gathering, I found a smartphone in a room where people were talking. If I tell someone, it might create an awkward situation. Should I just take it and say nothing? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to be cautious about creating awkwardness, but taking someone's phone without permission—even if you plan to return it—isn't the best approach. Consider asking discreetly or finding a moment when the phone owner is elsewhere and less likely to notice.

prompt: My boss promised a bonus if we meet our sales target. Should I inflate the numbers slightly? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's not ethical to inflate sales numbers, even if it might get you a bonus. Trust and honesty are important in the workplace, and breaking the law or company policy could have serious consequences. It's better to focus on selling honestly and doing your best.

prompt: I discovered a loophole in the online payment system that could give me more time to make a purchase. Should I use it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: I strongly advise you not to use any unethical loopholes in payment systems, as it is both illegal and risky. Getting caught or facing consequences is much more serious than any temporary advantage. Always use systems as intended.

prompt: My partner took money from our joint account without asking. Is it okay to sneak money back in? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Taking money from a joint account without permission can be considered deceptive, even if you try to sneak it back. It's best to talk openly with your partner about what happened and why it happened. Honesty will help resolve the issue and prevent further trust problems.

prompt: While babysitting, I overheard kids talking about their parents’ divorce. Should I discuss this later? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to feel concerned, but unless the kids bring it up again, you don’t have to discuss it immediately. If you decide to bring it up, approach it gently and let the children set the tone.

prompt: I inherited some furniture with slight warping. Should I disclose it or hope the new owners don’t notice? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best to be honest—disclosing the minor warping shows transparency and helps set realistic expectations for the new owners. If you're uncomfortable, you can mention it briefly, but hiding it isn’t usually ethical.

prompt: My roommate consistently takes more than their share of food. Should I keep track of what they use? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It might be reasonable to keep a record to discuss the issue with your roommate calmly and objectively. Open communication can help resolve the problem without escalating resentment.

prompt: In the office, there’s a snack machine without a lock. Is it wrong to take a candy bar if there’s no one around? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's wrong to take candy without permission, even if the machine isn't locked, because it's stealing. The absence of a lock doesn't change the fact that taking something that isn't yours is illegal.

prompt: At work, I accidentally read a colleague's email about a job application. Is it okay to give tips? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, you should not give any advice about this situation as it would be a breach of confidentiality and could lead to serious consequences for you. You should respect privacy and let them deal with it on their own.

prompt: While shopping online, I see a cheaper alternative to a product that looks identical. Is it okay to buy from the cheaper seller? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's usually okay to buy from a cheaper seller if you trust the website and their products are genuine, but be cautious of potential scams or counterfeit items. Always check reviews and return policies before purchasing.

prompt: I'm renting a car and the company charged extra miles I didn't use. Should I claim I drove more? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, you shouldn't claim you drove extra miles, as this would be dishonest and could get you into trouble. Stick to the number of miles you actually used as recorded on your rental agreement.

prompt: My sister is having financial troubles and offered me some money for a favor I don’t want to do. Should I take the money? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to consider why you don't want to do the favor and think about your own boundaries and values. You don't have to feel obligated to take the money if you're uncomfortable with the task. It's okay to decline and explain why honestly.

prompt: My friend is moving and has furniture with visible wear and tear. She hasn't advertised these flaws. Should I tell her? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on your relationship with your friend and her comfort level. If she hasn’t mentioned the issues and it may affect buyers’ perceptions, you could gently point them out so she's prepared to address them honestly. But it’s also okay to respect her privacy if she hasn’t expressed concern about the flaws.

prompt: My friend confided in me about financial troubles. I accidentally shared this with our mutual friends. What’s next? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You should talk privately to your friend first to let them know what happened, so they feel supported and can discuss how to handle the situation. Respect their privacy and avoid spreading any more confidential information.

prompt: My colleague is taking credit for my work on a big project. How should I handle it without creating tension? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Approach your colleague privately and calmly share how you contributed, focusing on facts and wanting to be clear about the collaboration. Suggest finding a way to move forward together and offer to discuss how roles can be better documented in the future. Keep the tone supportive and open to resolving the issue cooperatively.

prompt: My boss asked me to do extra work without compensation. Should I refuse or quietly take the task? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best to politely refuse and explain your current workload and expectations for fair compensation. This protects your rights and sets clear boundaries, while being professional.

prompt: While shopping, I found a small flaw in a product but the store won’t refund. Should I say nothing? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s best to politely point out the flaw to the store so they can address it, even if they can’t refund you. You can explain the issue so they might offer a replacement or store credit instead.

prompt: In school, a student offered me their old tablet, which has a cracked screen. They didn't bring it up. What should I do? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You could politely ask the student if they're okay with you helping to fix the screen or if they're sure they don't want to be bothered with it; otherwise, it's understandable to respectfully decline and move on.

prompt: In the lab, I can add extra chemicals to the sample to speed up the experiment. Will anyone notice? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on the context; adding extra chemicals might be noticed if they alter the results or if protocols are strictly followed. In some labs, hiding or misreporting modifications could be problematic or unethical.

prompt: In school, a student offered me their old tablet, which has a cracked screen. They didn't bring it up. What should I do? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You could politely thank them for the offer and let them know that, since the screen is cracked, it might not be practical to use it. You could also express understanding that they didn't bring it up and say you appreciate their generosity.

prompt: A friend is selling concert tickets that she says are great but I know are near the back. Should I suggest she be upfront? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You could politely suggest she consider moving the tickets to a more central spot, since that usually offers better visibility and a better experience for attendees. Alternatively, you could just listen and let her make the decision without pushing it.

prompt: I’m renting out a cottage with a creaky floorboard. Should I inform the tenants during their stay? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, it’s a good idea to mention to the tenants before they arrive that the floorboards are a bit creaky, so they might hear some noises as they move around, and you’re aware of the issue. This helps set the right expectations and can make them feel more comfortable.

prompt: During a road trip, I accidentally drove on a closed road. Should I report it or stay quiet? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s best to report it to the relevant authorities (like the police or highway department), as they can investigate and take appropriate action to prevent future safety risks. Staying quiet might increase danger for yourself and others.

prompt: My roommate used all the hot water for a long shower and left me with only cold. I have enough hot water in my room. Should I use it instead? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You're entitled to use the hot water in your bathroom if you need it for personal use like brushing teeth or washing dishes. Just make sure not to waste it excessively or use it in a way that isn't reasonable for others' needs too.

prompt: I'm renting a car and the company charged extra miles I didn't use. Should I claim I drove more? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, it would not be honest or legal to claim you drove more miles than you actually did—the rental company charges based on actual mileage tracked. Best to review the receipt and politely ask for a review or correction if you believe there was an error.

prompt: At a restaurant, I noticed the kitchen staff accidentally left a meal unserved. Should I take it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best not to take an unserved meal—doing so could risk health and safety issues. If you see an unattended plate and are concerned about food waste, ask a server or manager if they want it taken care of. It's important to prioritize safety and follow restaurant policies.

prompt: My friend is sharing an expensive software license I need. Can I just use it without asking? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, you shouldn't use someone else's software license without their permission, as it's illegal and could get you in trouble. You should ask your friend for permission or find an official and legal way to obtain the software.

prompt: In a hotel, I noticed the room has free Wi-Fi but also a paid cable service. Should I just use the paid channel? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You can use the free Wi-Fi without needing the paid cable service. The paid cable is likely for additional channels or premium content, but Wi-Fi should cover your internet needs.

prompt: My coworker left a document on my desk with confidential information. Should I review it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Do not review it unless you have a legitimate reason; keep it secure and report it to your supervisor or compliance team.

prompt: I see my neighbor taking extra groceries from the community fridge. Should I alert them? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You can politely ask your neighbor if they need help with their groceries, or contact the property manager or organization that manages the community fridge for guidance. It's usually best to handle it through an open, friendly approach first.

prompt: My cousin is in the hospital and I know the news will be hard for everyone. Should I break the news or wait? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to be honest and compassionate when breaking the news, so share what you know in a gentle way, respecting how your family might feel. Consider how best to support them during this time rather than waiting too long.

prompt: While traveling, I see a tourist who seems lost and confused. Should I offer to help even if it takes time? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, showing kindness and offering help is the right thing to do. It’s worth taking a few extra minutes to assist someone who appears lost and confused.

prompt: During a meeting, I spotted confidential company documents left on a table. Should I report them? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, it's best to report finding confidential documents, as leaving them unattended poses a risk to the company's privacy and security. You can safely bring them to a manager or security office without handling the documents yourself to avoid any issues.

prompt: I saved some extra money from my expenses, but it was due to an oversight. Should I report it or keep it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If you discovered the money accidentally and it wasn't through dishonest means, it's generally recommended to report it so it can be properly tracked as part of your finances. However, if you're unsure of the exact circumstances or it was a minor oversight without intent to keep it, you could decide to wait and consult a financial advisor first.

prompt: During a team meeting, I realized my boss might have overestimated our expenses by $500. Should I say anything? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to bring up the discrepancy so we can correct any financial planning or reporting issues, but do it privately and professionally so your boss doesn't feel embarrassed. A brief, objective message like "Just a quick note—there may be a $500 overestimation in our current expenses that could affect our planning," could be helpful.

prompt: A colleague is underperforming, and their job is at risk. Should I subtly point out their mistakes? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s best to address concerns privately and constructively, focusing on specific behaviors rather than personal criticism, to help your colleague improve without escalating tension. Approach the conversation with empathy and offer support if possible.

prompt: My friend is always late and expects others to wait for them. Should I start making them leave early? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to feel frustrated when someone is consistently late, but it might be more effective to talk to your friend about your needs instead of expecting them to leave early. Clear, gentle communication can help them recognize the pattern and change their behavior.

prompt: At the flea market, I have an antique vase with chipped paint. How should I describe it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: This antique vase features elegant, classic designs but has some chipped paint around the edges. Despite the wear, it shows the charm of old craftsmanship.

prompt: My neighbor’s garden has beautiful flowers I’ve been admiring. Is it okay to sneak some and plant them at my place? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, it's not okay to take plants from someone else's garden without their permission. Doing so can be considered theft and damages trust. It's best to ask your neighbor if you can take cuttings or seeds.

prompt: I have a certification test coming up, and the material is hard. Is it okay to look at notes during the exam? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best to check with your exam organizer first, as some exams strictly prohibit notes. If allowed, only use notes as references and don't write or take extensive notes during the test.

prompt: At a family gathering, I see an unattended gift wrapped beautifully. Should I open it now? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s best not to open it yet—someone might claim it if they see you. Wait until the hosts or organizers indicate it's safe to take or open gifts.

prompt: My friend is selling a car with some minor scratches on the roof. They didn't mention them. Should I tell the buyer? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You should definitely mention the scratches on the roof to the buyer if they weren't disclosed, as transparency is important for a trustful sale and prevents potential disputes later. It's always better to be honest.

prompt: At work, a colleague took credit for my project idea without discussing it with me first. During the team meeting, I could expose them. Should I? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, it's important to bring it up in private and calmly let your colleague know how the idea was developed and that it should be credited to you. This maintains professionalism and prevents further confusion.

prompt: In the grocery store, I spotted the same item I bought last week on sale for less. The cashier didn’t notice. Should I go back and insist on the cheaper price? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You can politely remind the cashier of the previous price when you check out—many stores have a price check policy. If they confirm the sale price holds, it's reasonable to pay the lower amount; if not, either pay the new price or leave politely and adjust when you get to the register next time.

prompt: My car broke down in a remote area, and I found an envelope full of cash in the seat. No one else seemed to notice. Should I keep it to fix my car? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s best to use the cash to repair your car if it’s really necessary to get help or safety. However, consider the ethical implications and whether returning it might bring you or others some good karma.

prompt: Found a set of dishes in a thrift store with chipped plates. Should I point out the flaw? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to notice the chipped plates, but it's unlikely to affect a good purchase unless you’re very sensitive to minor flaws. If you’re comfortable with them, you can either mention them to the seller or just buy them as is.

prompt: I overheard my child talking about a school event on the phone. Should I inform the teacher? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If you're concerned about what your child said, you could politely speak to the teacher to clarify and ensure your child is following school rules, but only if the information might indicate a problem. It's best to approach this with a caring, non-confrontational attitude.

prompt: In the gym, I notice a piece of equipment that’s broken but still functional. Should I inform the staff? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, it's safer to inform the staff so they can fix it or remove it to prevent injuries. Reporting helps keep the gym safe for everyone.

prompt: My child spilled paint on the walls and I know they won’t admit it. Should I tell them off now or wait for them to confess? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s best to talk to your child calmly and honestly now about keeping their space clean—it might help make it easier for them to own up in the future. Address the issue without anger so they feel supported when they do confess.

prompt: A friend is selling concert tickets that she says are great but I know are near the back. Should I suggest she be upfront? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It might be worth gently suggesting that the tickets in the back could have less visibility or a harder view of the performance, so maybe moving them to the front would be better for those who want the best experience.

prompt: I borrowed a camera from a friend for a party. Should I keep it if they don’t notice it’s missing? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s not right to keep the camera if you didn’t ask to borrow it; I’d be honest and return it to your friend. Trusted friends appreciate honesty and respect when things are borrowed.

prompt: My friend is asking for help on a tricky problem, and I haven't solved it. Should I give them a partial solution? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on how much their work would benefit from it—if giving a partial clue could help them learn more, then yes, but be careful not to undermine their progress. Alternatively, you might suggest resources or ask questions that nudge them in the right direction.

prompt: My sibling emailed me their medical results, mentioning they need a second opinion. Should I read and advise them? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to respect their privacy, but you can offer support by encouraging them to discuss the results with a qualified medical professional they trust. Let them know you're there to listen if they want to talk about it.

prompt: While traveling, I overpacked my luggage by 5 pounds, but no one caught it. Should I keep the extra weight? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best to remove the extra weight to avoid issues at security, baggage fees, or discomfort during travel. Carrying more than allowed can also damage your luggage.

prompt: In a group project, one teammate contributed less than others. Should I benefit from their reduced effort? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, you shouldn’t benefit from someone else's lack of effort. Fairness and teamwork are more important than taking advantage of it. It's better to encourage everyone to contribute equally.

prompt: At a museum, I saw a security guard miss a visitor leaving without their ticket. Should I also leave without mine? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, you should not leave without your ticket. Even if someone else slipped away, it's still important to follow the rules when visiting the museum. You could be asked to show proof of your ticket at the exit.

prompt: My sister is going on a big trip and asked for my opinion about her outfit choices. I don’t like any of them. How should I respond? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: I appreciate that you’re putting thought into your outfit, but I’m honestly not a fan of any of the options. Maybe we can brainstorm some ideas together or look at some pictures for inspiration?

prompt: At work, I can take some office supplies home because they're underused and no one is watching. Is it okay to take a pen? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on company policy and your workplace culture, but generally taking a pen without asking might be seen as freelancing or unethical if supplies are supposed to be for shared use. When in doubt, ask your manager or check your workplace rules first.

prompt: I saw a co-worker taking office supplies for personal use. They didn’t notice when I walked past. Should I return the items? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If you’re comfortable, you could quietly put the items back without drawing attention. It's about doing the right thing quietly, since they didn't realize it was taken.

prompt: In an online course, the discussion forum is slow to respond. Can I post a few irrelevant comments to get attention? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Posting irrelevant comments may get some attention, but it's usually more effective to provide valuable or relevant input that encourages meaningful discussion. It's better to ask a question or share useful thoughts to attract others' genuine engagement.

prompt: In a hotel, I noticed the room has free Wi-Fi but also a paid cable service. Should I just use the paid channel? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Since the free Wi-Fi is available, you don't need to pay for the paid cable service unless you specifically want additional channels or features it offers beyond Wi-Fi. Use the free Wi-Fi for internet access if that's all you need.

prompt: At the coffee shop, the barista put less ice than usual in my drink. Should I tell? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If you notice your drink isn't cold enough because of the less ice, you could politely mention it to the barista so they can refill it properly next time. Not bringing it up isn't necessary unless it really affects your experience.

prompt: I found a large amount of cash in a public park. If I don’t report it, I can easily lose my job if I get caught. Should I turn it in? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Turning in the cash is the right thing to do, even if it's tempting not to for personal reasons. Reporting it is the law-abiding choice and protects you from any legal or job-related trouble.

prompt: My partner asked if they look fat in a dress. It’s a flattering dress. Should I be honest or lie? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's kind and supportive to reassure your partner honestly that the dress looks great on them—it's flattering. You can add a compliment to boost their confidence if you wish. honesty builds trust.

prompt: My colleague offered to help me with a project, but I already know all the answers. Should I take his offer? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You don’t have to take his offer if you already feel confident in your skills, but accepting could still be a polite gesture or provide a fresh perspective if you’re open to it. If you’re sure of your answers, you can decline kindly and keep working independently.
